title: Merge K Sorted Lists
description:
You are given lists, an array of zero or more singly linked chains. To express multiple chains in JSON, each input chain is supplied as an array of its values, in head-to-tail order; an empty array denotes an empty chain. Every chain is individually sorted in nondecreasing order. Return a single linked-chain head containing all values in nondecreasing order, including duplicates.

The input can contain zero chains or any number of empty chains, in which case return a null head (serialized as null). Return a ListNode head, not a flat array: the grader serializes nonempty returned chains into the output arrays shown below. Construct nodes from the supplied per-chain arrays when you need to manipulate links, or merge directly from their current indices.

The interesting trade-off is between repeatedly searching all current heads and selecting the next smallest efficiently. A heap of current candidates or pairwise merging makes many short chains manageable. Never assume the first list always supplies the next smallest element, and retain all equal values.

Example 1:

Input: lists = [[1,4,5],[1,3,4],[2,6]]
Output: [1,1,2,3,4,4,5,6]

Example 2:

Input: lists = []
Output: null

Example 3:

Input: lists = [[],[1,2],[],[3]]
Output: [1,2,3]

Constraints:

  • 0 <= lists.length <= 100.
  • 0 <= length of each chain <= 100.
  • -10,000 <= node.val <= 10,000.
  • Each inner array represents one sorted chain.
